key_insight: Non-dimensionalization can determine PINN trainability: free-fall scaling reduces the buoyancy-driven gradient imbalance that undermines thermal-diffusive scaling.
engineering_relevance: Choosing appropriate physical scales before training can improve PINN reliability for buoyancy-driven heat-transfer prediction.
method: Study a differentially heated square cavity at Pr = 0.71 and Ra = 10³–10⁵.
Compare thermal-diffusive and free-fall scalings under identical training conditions.
Measure loss gradients and test sparse-data supervision and adaptive loss weighting.
evidence_signal: Free-fall scaling yields mean Nusselt-number errors below 1.1% for Ra ≤ 10⁴, versus 157–650% for diffusive scaling, which diverges at Ra = 10⁵.
watch_item: Free-fall scaling does not resolve all failures: the unsteady PINN misses the transient Nusselt-number overshoot despite accurate long-time heat transfer.
paper_title: Inherent Failure Modes of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Buoyancy-Driven Flow: Role of Non-Dimensionalization in Network Training
